GREEN TECHNOLOGY PORTABLE AIR CONDITIONER

Turning a conventional air cooler into a portable air conditioner by reusing existing components. A practical approach to reducing e-waste, electricity consumption and equipment cost.

01 / Introduction

A smarter second life for cooling equipment.

This project converts a conventional air cooler into a portable air conditioner by reusing existing components. The conversion extends equipment lifespan, reduces e-waste and improves cooling performance with minimal energy consumption.

Project concept

Reuse suitable components from existing cooling appliances to develop a functioning portable air-conditioning prototype.

Design priorities

Cooling capability, electrical performance, cost awareness, airflow and operational stability are the primary evaluation areas.

02 / Problem statement

Three problems. One project response.

The following statements and references are reproduced from the exhibition poster.

♻️

Electronic waste (E-waste)

  • Increase of e-waste from discarded cooling appliances.
  • Many end-of-life air coolers are thrown away although components still function.
Journal / source stated on posterAnnals of Global Health, Vol. 80, Issue 4, July–August 2014, pages 286–295.
⚡

Electricity consumption

  • Portable air conditioners require high electricity during long operation.
  • This increases operating cost for regular users.
Reference stated on posterHalimi, Nur Auji Najlaa (2020).
◎

Equipment cost

  • Portable air conditioners are costly and not easily affordable.
  • Better low-cost cooling alternatives are needed.
Journal / source stated on posterSreyas International Journal of Scientists and Technocrats, Vol. 3(1), 2019, pp. 14–23.

Reference details are shown as printed on the poster. Full article titles, authors and links were not provided on the poster.

03 / Project objectives

All nine project objectives.

Each member is responsible for three measurable objectives, as specified in the project poster.

ARMAND · 3 OBJECTIVES
01Measure cooling capacity.
02Measure noise level.
03Identify and quantify reused components.
SYAFIQ · 3 OBJECTIVES
04Calculate COP based on ASHRAE.
05Calculate total energy usage (kWh).
06Test 2–4 hours operation with ±2°C stability.
HASBULLAH · 3 OBJECTIVES
07Measure airflow rate at 2–4 meters.
08Measure power consumption (target 500–700 W).
09Evaluate condenser water spray effect.
